title: Enhancing Measures to Prevent Sexual Harassment in Schools and Institutes of Higher Learning
what_it_is: Enhancing Measures to Prevent Sexual Harassment in Schools and Institutes of Higher Learning

sections.label: Sexual harassment measures in institutions
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister for Education about measures, reviews, shortcomings, improvements and training on sexual harassment in autonomous universities and polytechnics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) what measures were put in place to reduce sexual harassment and misconduct in autonomous universities and polytechnics after reports of sexualised harassment during orientation activities in 2016; (b) what steps were taken to review these measures subsequently; (c) what were the shortcomings; (d) what steps have been taken to improve; and (e) what further steps are planned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) what are the forms of training provided at educational institutions to address sexual harassment and assault cases, including support for victims; (b) what are the measures to support victims; (c) what are the policies pertaining to investigating allegations of sexual harassment and assault; and (d) what are the procedures in place to review the effectiveness of such measures and to propose improvements.

sections.label: NUS victim support shortcomings
sections.summary: The case reported by NUS student Monica Baey shows shortcomings in victim support and lacking areas at NUS.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The recent case reported by National University of Singapore (NUS) student Monica Baey shows that insofar as NUS is concerned, there were shortcomings in victim support and there were clearly areas which were lacking.

sections.label: Victim Care Unit established
sections.summary: One immediate step is the establishment of a Victim Care Unit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: One of the immediate steps is the establishment of a Victim Care Unit.

sections.label: NUS hostel restroom installations
sections.summary: NUS began installing full-height doors and partitions in hostel and sports facility restrooms and new locks at hostel restroom entrances.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Over this past week, NUS started installing full-height doors and partitions in the restrooms of all its hostels and sports facilities, as well as new locks at the entrances of the hostel restrooms.

sections.label: SUSS security staff camera training
sections.summary: SUSS is collaborating with the Singapore Police Force to train security staff to inspect toilet cubicles or ceilings for cameras.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: For example, SUSS is collaborating with the Singapore Police Force to train its security staff to inspect toilet cubicles or ceilings for such cameras.

sections.label: Respect consent course, Penal Code update
sections.summary: IHLs will strengthen education, NUS will introduce a respect and consent course, and the Penal Code is being updated for technology-enabled sex crimes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The IHLs are committed to this and will be taking steps to strengthen such education.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: For instance, NUS will be introducing a course on respect and consent at the start of the new academic year for all students, faculty and staff.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: With image-capturing devices becoming ubiquitous, especially on mobile phones, such crimes are no longer contained between the victim and perpetrator, and the potential for mass dissemination is much higher.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We are updating the Penal Code to deal with technology-enabled sex crimes.

sections.label: Organisations adapting to sexual misconduct norms
sections.summary: All organisations must keep up with changing norms, signal that sexual misconduct is unacceptable and handle complaints appropriately.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: As societal norms and expectations change, all organisations need to keep up with the times, send clear signals that sexual misconduct is unacceptable and equip themselves to deal with sexual misconduct complaints appropriately should they arise.

sections.label: Voyeurism at autonomous universities
sections.summary: At the AUs, about two-thirds of cases are voyeurism, with no rising trend in the last three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: At the AUs, the big bulk, about two-thirds, is still voyeurism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Based on the data I gave just now, there has not been a rising trend in the last three years.

sections.label: NUS framework review timing
sections.summary: NUS' framework was reviewed about five years ago and was probably due for review.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: NUS' framework was reviewed about five years ago, and it was probably due for review.

sections.label: Publicity and penalties for misconduct
sections.summary: The framework is on the student website, past cases were reported, but penalties are not stiff enough.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: It is available on their student website, which is why after the latest incident, there were several press reports about past cases, because it was publicly available within the NUS website.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I think we can publicise but, fundamentally, as what I have mentioned, the penalties are just not stiff enough.

sections.label: IHLs reviewing security arrangements
sections.summary: All IHLs are reviewing security arrangements, with NUS already started and completion expected in coming months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The short answer is that all the IHLs are reviewing their security arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In the case of NUS, they have already embarked on it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: They are expected to be completed in the coming months.

sections.label: Counsellor training and AU autonomy
sections.summary: Minimum standards for counsellor training are questioned, while respecting AUs' independent boards separate from MOE.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Last but not least, what would be some of the minimum standards on training and imparting of skills for the counsellors dealing with this sensitive matter of people being subjected to sexual harassment?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I think we also need to respect the fact that they are AUs having their own boards and governing themselves in a fairly independent way, separate from MOE.

sections.label: Public statement on inadequate penalties
sections.summary: The speaker says that after issuing a public statement that penalties are manifestly inadequate, everyone understood the standard being sought.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Having said that, when I first issued my public statement that the penalties are manifestly inadequate, I think they all understood the standard that I was looking for.

sections.label: Suspension differences across universities
sections.summary: The concern is that conduct attracting a suspension in one university might only attract a reprimand or expulsion in another.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The concern here is that what attracts a suspension in one university might only attract a reprimand or expulsion in another.

sections.label: Disciplinary committees' expertise and skills
sections.summary: There is concern that disciplinary committees may lack the right expertise or skills for all their functions, as they are not the Police or Attorney-General's Chambers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The second question is: when we look at the disciplinary committees, there is some concern that they may not have the right expertise or skills to discharge all of their functions because, frankly, they are not the Police or the Attorney-General's Chambers.

sections.label: Inconsistencies across AUs
sections.summary: On the first question of inconsistencies across AUs, the speaker says he would not call it inconsistencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The first question of inconsistencies across AUs, I would not call it inconsistencies.

sections.label: Members of disciplinary boards
sections.summary: The disciplinary boards of the review committees will need to have certain members, including student representatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The disciplinary boards of the review committees will need to have certain members, including having student representatives.
